purpose: Everything a line-of-business application would otherwise build for itself, resolved at compile time. Install the package for what you need and write one Add call.
readThisFirst: Before writing a foundational abstraction — caching, validation, a repository, a result type, a pipeline — check this catalog. If Zero has it, use it. Writing a second one is the mistake this framework exists to prevent.

capabilities.title: Validated configuration
capabilities.useWhen: Any time the application reads a setting.

capabilities.title: Authorization
capabilities.useWhen: A request may only be made by some callers. Do not check permissions inside a handler, and do not write your own policy or claims abstraction.

capabilities.title: Caching
capabilities.useWhen: A read is expensive and a slightly stale answer is acceptable. Do not cache inside a handler and do not write your own cache abstraction or key builder.

capabilities.title: Commands, queries and the pipeline
capabilities.useWhen: The application has use cases. Do not write your own mediator or dispatcher, and do not call a handler directly.

capabilities.title: Logging, tracing and metrics
capabilities.useWhen: You need to see what the application is doing. Do not log, trace or time inside a handler.

capabilities.title: Data access
capabilities.useWhen: The application stores things. Do not write your own repository or specification abstraction, and do not put provider-specific query calls in a handler.

capabilities.title: Entity Framework provider
capabilities.useWhen: The application stores things in a relational database through Entity Framework.

capabilities.title: Results and errors
capabilities.useWhen: An operation can fail in a way the caller should handle. Do not write your own Result, Either or Maybe type.

capabilities.title: Testing a Zero application
capabilities.useWhen: Writing tests for handlers, validators or a whole application. Do not hand-build a service provider or a dispatch table in a test.

capabilities.title: Request validation
capabilities.useWhen: A request has rules about what it may contain. Do not validate inside a handler.

capabilities.title: HTTP endpoints
capabilities.useWhen: Commands and queries need to be reachable over HTTP. Do not write controllers or your own result-to-status-code mapping.

capabilities.title: Domain events
capabilities.useWhen: One thing happening should cause several others, and the caller does not need their answers. Do not write your own event bus or notification dispatcher.

capabilities.title: Recurring work
capabilities.useWhen: Work has to happen on a clock rather than on a request. Do not write an IHostedService with a while loop and a Task.Delay.

capabilities.title: Retrying what is worth retrying
capabilities.useWhen: A dependency is sometimes unavailable. Do not write a retry loop in a handler, and do not reach for a policy that fires on exceptions -- a Zero failure is a returned value.
